name: frame_clock
summary: FPS is constant time data. FrameClock pins any continuous timestamp to integer frame indices at canonical FPSes (24/30/60/90/120). Gives the chain lossless integer joins, cross-substrate sync (Godot frame N = Remotion frame N = SpriteForge frame N = spatial_anchor scan N), and compact tamper-evident hex storage. The discrete-time twin of tri_modal_embedder.time_vector.
engine_pattern: deterministic floor(timestamp * fps) at multiple FPSes. Pack as 8-byte big-endian uint64s → hex. Crystal = BLAKE3 over canonical (fps_set + frames + rounded timestamp).

inbound_callers: (planned) inference_logger.log — every record gets frames dict + frame_clock_hex

smoke_test_results_2026_05_28.round_trip_hex: identical ts and frames after to_hex → from_hex
smoke_test_results_2026_05_28.frame_sync_retrieval: tolerance=1 frame at 60fps correctly clusters godot+remotion+spriteforge events

the_three_gains: 1. INTEGER JOINS — 'all events at frame N at FPS X' is O(1) per record (dict lookup, not float distance)
2. CROSS-SUBSTRATE SYNC — Godot _process(delta) frame N = Remotion comp frame N = SpriteForge sheet frame N = spatial_anchor scan N
3. TAMPER-EVIDENT — recompute frame indices from timestamp; mismatch = corrupted. Differential-amplifier at the time axis.
guarantees: Deterministic — same timestamp → same frame tuple, byte-exact across runs
Lossless integer rescale — convert_frame(1800, 30, 60) = 3600, no float drift at exact multiples
Compact storage — 5 uint64s = 40 bytes = 80 hex chars per FrameClock
Pure stdlib — no numpy, no dateutil
usage_example:
from frame_clock import FrameClock, find_synced_records
c = FrameClock.now()
print(c.frames)  # {24: ..., 30: ..., 60: ..., 90: ..., 120: ...}
# Find all chain events frame-synced to this moment at 60fps within 1 frame:
synced = find_synced_records(c, my_chain_corpus, tolerance_frames=1, fps=60)
